clinician.final_diagnosis: Thyrotoxicosis secondary to autoimmune thyroiditis induced by immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) treatment, presenting as delirium with cognitive and systemic manifestations
clinician.trajectory_summary: 64-year-old female with pleural mesothelioma initiated on nivolumab and ipilimumab for locoregional progression. Coinciding with immunotherapy initiation, she developed a 2-month progressive syndrome of cognitive disturbances (disorientation, inattention, forgetfulness, confusion, sporadic nocturnal visual hallucinations, naming difficulties) accompanied by systemic symptoms (asthenia, adynamia, gait instability, heat intolerance, nocturnal sweating, palpitations, tremors, low mood). On admission workup, thyroid function tests revealed thyrotoxicosis with elevated peripheral thyroid hormones (total T4 and T3) and suppressed TSH. Thyroid serology demonstrated anti-thyroglobulin antibodies with negative TRAb and TPO antibodies, consistent with autoimmune thyroiditis. Brain MRI excluded structural causes (no vascular lesions or mesothelioma dissemination, only non-confluent supratentorial white matter microangiopathy). Beta-blocker symptomatic treatment was initiated, leading to gradual amelioration of neurological manifestations. At discharge, the patient was scheduled for outpatient endocrinology monitoring and continued on her oncological regimen without modifications.
